minutes.headline: School Committee met with a search consultant to plan the superintendent search, timetable and job profile; no formal votes.
minutes.summary: The committee met with a consultant from the Massachusetts Association of School Committees to set up the search for a new superintendent. They discussed a search committee's makeup, a timetable for applications, interviews and site visits, how to solicit letters of interest, and edited the job description and criteria. The only formal motion captured was to adjourn.

budget_items.what_was_said: The consultant said districts either set a compensation range or advertise a competitive salary, and the committee should decide. Later the committee leaned toward salary commensurate with experience.

decisions.decision: Solicit letters of interest for the search committee from community, with roles and date availability, posted widely and via principals.
Search committee meeting dates set as April 30, May 3, May 7, May 10, 12, 14 and 16, with the committee appointed at the 25th meeting.
Job criteria to require ten years in education, keeping it flexible; bullets to be drawn from other districts' samples.
Search committee meetings will not begin before six o'clock.

what_happened.line: The School Committee met with a search consultant from the Massachusetts Association of School Committees to plan the search for a new superintendent; no formal votes were taken.
The committee agreed to solicit letters of interest for the search committee from the community, with roles and date availability, posted widely and through principals.
Search committee meeting dates were set informally for late April through mid-May, with the committee to be appointed at the 25th meeting.
Search committee meetings will not begin before six o'clock.
The job criteria will require ten years in education while staying flexible, with bullets drawn from other districts' samples.

why_it_matters: The superintendent leads the district's schools and proposes its budget, so the profile and process set now shape who is hired and how the search is run.
Residents can apply to sit on the search committee, and evening meeting times are meant to make that possible for people who work days.
